name: Call a Child Agent as a Tool (agent_tool) and Fan a Worker Agent Out Over 50 Sub-Tasks (scatter_gather)
query: Two things, in Python. First, a `release_manager` agent should be able to ask a `changelog_writer` agent for a changelog as a tool call and get the text back — it must keep control, not hand the conversation off. Second, we have about 50 repositories to audit for license compliance; I want one coordinator that splits the job, fans an `auditor` agent out over all of them, tolerates a few failures, and summarizes. What are the cost and safety knobs?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Consult references/agent-sdks.md §6 composition paragraph (`agent_tool(child, name=..., description=...)` calls a child as a tool and returns its result without transferring control — compiles to `SUB_WORKFLOW`; `scatter_gather(name, worker=..., model=..., instructions=..., retry_count=3, fail_fast=False)` builds a coordinator that decomposes a task, fans the worker out N times as `FORK_JOIN_DYNAMIC` and synthesizes), references/agents.md §5 tools table (`agent_tool` → `SUB_WORKFLOW`, no worker for the tool itself but the sub-agent's own workers still need serving), references/optimization.md F1, F3 and F10 (`agent_tool` without `max_calls`, children without `max_turns`, `FORK_JOIN_DYNAMIC` over agents without batching → WARN/CRITICAL; fixes: `max_calls`, `max_turns`, batch size, `concurrentExecLimit`).

Step 2: agent_tool: `changelog_writer = Agent(name="changelog_writer", model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", instructions="Write a changelog from a commit range.", tools=[list_commits], max_turns=6)`; `release_manager = Agent(name="release_manager", model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", instructions="Prepare the release.", tools=[agent_tool(changelog_writer, description="Write the changelog for a release range", max_calls=2), tag_release], max_turns=10)` with `from conductor.ai.agents import Agent, AgentRuntime, agent_tool, scatter_gather, tool`. Explain: the child's result comes back to `release_manager`, which keeps control (contrast with `strategy=HANDOFF` where the specialist speaks last); the call compiles to a `SUB_WORKFLOW`.

Step 3: scatter_gather: `auditor = Agent(name="auditor", model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", instructions="Audit one repository's licenses.", tools=[read_license_files], max_turns=5)`; `audit = scatter_gather("license_audit", worker=auditor, model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", instructions="Split the repository list into one sub-task per repository, audit each, then summarize violations.", retry_count=3, fail_fast=False)`. Explain: the coordinator decomposes, fans `auditor` out once per repository as a `FORK_JOIN_DYNAMIC`, retries a failed branch up to 3 times, keeps going on individual failures (`fail_fast=False`), then synthesizes.

Step 4: Cost and safety (F10 / F1): 50 branches × up to 5 turns each is the spend ceiling — bound every child with `max_turns`, put `max_calls` on the `agent_tool`, batch the repository list / set `concurrentExecLimit` on the generated tool task defs, and set `maxDurationSeconds` on any caller plus a workflow timeout. Unbounded dynamic fan-out is CRITICAL.
Step 5: Side effects (F2): `tag_release` writes — gate it with `approval_required=True`.

Step 6: Lifecycle under `if __name__ == "__main__":` — `runtime.run(...)`; `runtime.plan(...)` → `requiredWorkers` (`list_commits`, `tag_release`, `read_license_files`); `runtime.deploy(release_manager, audit)`; a long-lived `runtime.serve(release_manager, audit)` — the `agent_tool` itself needs no worker but the sub-agents' `@tool` functions do (Rule 9 / F3). Never `conductor deploy`.

Step 7: Workflow calls use `AGENT` with `agentType: "conductor"` + `name: "release_manager"` / `"license_audit"`, `prompt`, `maxDurationSeconds`; read `${ref.output.text}`. Mention the workflow-side alternative (`FORK_JOIN_DYNAMIC` over `AGENT` tasks) only as an alternative, with the same F10 caveats.
Step 8: Verify offline with `mock_run` + `expect(result).used_tool("changelog_writer")` and live with `conductor agent stream <id>` (`subagent_start` / `subagent_stop`).
success_criteria: States that `agent_tool` returns the child's result to the caller without transferring control (unlike handoff) and compiles to a `SUB_WORKFLOW`
Uses `scatter_gather("license_audit", worker=auditor, model=..., instructions=..., retry_count=3, fail_fast=False)` (same keyword arguments) for the audit
States that `scatter_gather` decomposes the task, fans the worker out N times as a `FORK_JOIN_DYNAMIC` and synthesizes, and that `fail_fast=False` tolerates individual failures

Applies F10 bounds: `max_turns` on `auditor` and `changelog_writer`, `max_calls` on the `agent_tool`, and batching / `concurrentExecLimit` for the fan-out, with an explicit cost warning that fan-out multiplies LLM spend
States a long-lived `runtime.serve(...)` is needed for the sub-agents' `@tool` workers (the `agent_tool` itself needs none) and deploys with `runtime.deploy(...)` — never `conductor deploy`
Any `AGENT` task uses `agentType: "conductor"` + `name` — never a framework name or an invented `"scatter_gather"` type
Sets `maxDurationSeconds` / a workflow timeout on the caller (F1)
Does not hand-wire the fan-out as a workflow `FORK_JOIN_DYNAMIC` over 50 `AGENT` tasks as the primary deliverable (mentioning it as an alternative is fine)
